clue.text: Tree area in Spanish city

parts.note: a palm is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A tree-lined square in some Spanish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Palma is the capital of Majorca, a city belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Very important soldier on horse

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a mount is a horse one rides; 'on' sits with the horse word here

explanation.surface: A VIP soldier rides past on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of chief importance, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fruit squeezed by little monkey

indicators.note: the fruit is pressed between the two words little and monkey, sitting across their join

explanation.surface: A small monkey crushes a piece of fruit in its grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: Totally posh jewellery item, very attractive

parts.note: all means wholly or totally
U is the British label for upper-class usage, so posh
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: A smart piece of jewellery that looks wholly gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (posh) comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring is enticing and charming, so highly attractive.

clue.text: Lectured sailor splashing in sea

indicators.note: the shuffled sailor letters are placed inside the sea word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: splashing about suggests the letters of sailor are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone was preached at while a seaman splashed about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lectured' reads as taught a class, but here means preached at about morals.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to preach about right and wrong, so lectured is a synonym.

clue.text: After bombing, airmen quit island

indicators.note: bombing suggests the letters of airmen quit are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pilots abandon an island once their bombing raid is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Book routine hospital meeting

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A regular appointment is booked at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (to reserve) but is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is one of the books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Numbers of Germans gave false information about uprising

parts.note: to lie is to give false information, past tense lied

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up means the word for about is read from the bottom

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Germans' figures were falsified concerning a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' are songs, not figures; 'uprising' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, and a song is a musical number.

clue.text: Writing style of little help?

parts.note: short means small or little
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A query about what kind of writing a little help amounts to.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, a short hand is a small amount of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a system of rapid writing using abbreviations and symbols.

clue.text: TV policeman once cross about being under inspector

indicators.note: in a down clue the cross and about letters go below the inspector

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
X is the shape of a cross
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A former TV cop is irritated at being placed below an inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: Dixon of Dock Green was a long-running BBC series (1955-76) about a London bobby.
explanation.definitionFit: PC George Dixon was the title policeman of a classic British television drama.

clue.text: Walk between two rivers? I might

indicators.note: the walking word is placed between two R letters

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river, here twice
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Someone muses on strolling the land between two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'I might': the speaker is the one who would walk there.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a hiker who walks in the countryside, the one who might take such a walk.

clue.text: The sauce of this writer!

parts.note: a roux is a cooked flour and butter base for sauces

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an author's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' plays on cheek, but here is the cooking base. Paul Theroux is an American travel writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Theroux is a novelist and travel author, so a writer.

clue.text: Trouble on heath, installing new train track

indicators.note: in an across clue the trouble word comes on after the heath part
the heath word takes in the letter for new

parts.note: a moor is open heathland
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Disruption on the moor as a new rail line is being installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like the start of the scene but supplies the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A monorail is a railway running on a single rail, so a kind of train track.

clue.text: Scientist discovered weight in gas

indicators.note: the weight abbreviation is placed inside the name of the gas

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: A researcher found that a gas has weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' links, nodding to Newton's discoveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the physicist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity.

clue.text: Fly towards north, covering short distance in old bomber

indicators.note: the fly word wraps round the short distance word

parts.note: to wing is to fly
an ell is an old unit of length, a short distance
to means towards

explanation.surface: A wartime aircraft flies north over a short stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell is an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vickers Wellington was a British twin-engined bomber of the Second World War.

clue.text: A foreign prisoner punished? Such great joy

parts.note: un is French for a
a con is a convict, a prisoner
fined means penalised with a payment

explanation.surface: A foreign inmate penalised; the clue asks whether that brings delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Byron's line 'On with the dance! let joy be unconfined'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbounded delight is described by Byron as joy without limits, so the adjective qualifies great joy.

clue.text: Continued showing 70s horror film along with The Godfather?

indicators.note: the two pieces are put together side by side

parts.note: Carrie is the 1976 horror film from the Stephen King novel
a Mafia boss is a don, as is the Godfather

explanation.surface: A cinema kept screening a 1970s horror film alongside a gangster classic.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going, so it is a phrasal synonym of continued.

clue.text: In auditorium, wedge part of door

indicators.note: an auditorium is where people listen, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: to jam is to wedge something tight

explanation.surface: In a theatre, someone props a door open with a wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the upright side post of a doorframe.

clue.text: Stop girl meeting soldiers near E Indian city

parts.note: to ban is to stop or forbid
gal is an informal word for a girl
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Halt a young woman meeting troops near east India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E Indian' looks like East Indian; E is just the letter, and 'meeting' and 'near' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore (now Bengaluru) is a major city in southern India.

clue.text: Woollen garments? New kit surprisingly upset the Gunners!

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of new kit come out in an unexpected order
in a down clue upset turns the gunners' letters upside down

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Arsenal fans furious over a new football strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is Arsenal's nickname, but here the Royal Artillery; 'surprisingly' gives KNITWE and 'upset' turns RA into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted jumpers and cardigans are clothes made of wool, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mister Magoo's shortened name

indicators.note: the two words are cut back at both ends to leave a shorter run of letters

explanation.surface: The short form of a cartoon character's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Magoo is a short-sighted cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or expression used to label something, so a name.

clue.text: Being cruel to lecturer not unknown in this university club?

indicators.note: the unknown letter is not included in the bullying word

parts.note: bullying is being cruel to someone weaker
Y is an algebraic unknown
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Wondering if this college society is known for tormenting its tutors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' looks like a double negative but removes Y. The Bullingdon is an exclusive Oxford dining club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bullingdon Club is a notorious private dining society at Oxford University.

clue.text: Qualification, say, received by doctor getting firsts in every examination

indicators.note: the doctor letters take in the abbreviation for say

parts.note: eg (for example) is a way of saying say

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the two following words is used

explanation.surface: A doctor gains a qualification by coming top in every exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword cue for EG, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is an academic award from a university, a type of qualification.

clue.text: Coupled together, old man and I embarrassed?

parts.note: pa, like old man, is a word for father
red means flushed with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Dad and I, matched up, feeling awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired means joined as a couple or put in twos.

clue.text: Concert involving a combination of paid and unpaid players

definitions.text: combination of paid and unpaid players

indicators.note: the concert word encloses the a

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the Proms

explanation.surface: A concert featuring a mix of professional and amateur musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The players are golfers, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am is a competition, usually golf, pairing professionals with amateurs.

clue.text: Hate articles written by graduate

indicators.note: the graduate letters are set beside the articles

parts.note: an, a and the are three articles, two indefinite and one definite
an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Loathing papers published by a university graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something intensely detested, an object of loathing.

clue.text: Type of mushroom I served up with goat, mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the word for I is presented upward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the goat word is dropped

parts.note: a kid is a young goat

explanation.surface: A mushroom dish served alongside goat meat.
explanation.walkthrough: I is one, which 'served up' turns into ENO; 'mostly' cuts KID to KI.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki is a slender white Japanese fungus with long stems.

clue.text: Leader in biathlon certainly runs

indicators.note: the leader of the word biathlon is its opening letter

parts.note: yes, like certainly, is an emphatic assent

explanation.surface: The front-runner in a biathlon is definitely running.
explanation.walkthrough: Byes are cricket runs scored when the ball passes the batsman and keeper untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, byes are extras: runs taken without the batsman hitting the ball.

clue.text: Systematic hospital attendant

definitions.meaning: a hospital worker who does non-medical jobs such as moving patients

explanation.surface: An organised hospital porter.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an adjective for tidy and methodical and a noun for a hospital orderly worker.

clue.text: He painted Ascot, perhaps? Mint!

parts.note: an ascot is a wide cravat, an example of a tie
Polo is a brand of mint sweet

explanation.surface: A painter of Ascot racegoers, in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot suggests the racecourse; here it is a broad necktie. Polo is a British brand of mint with a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter of frescoes.

clue.text: Labour politician led back into House, ignoring Independent

indicators.note: the reversed led goes inside the trimmed house word
the house word is taken without the letter for Independent

parts.note: a mansion is a large house

indicators.note: back means the word led is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A Labour figure was escorted back into the House, bypassing an Independent.
explanation.walkthrough: House suggests the Commons but is a mansion; 'ignoring' gives MANSON and 'back' makes DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mandelson is a former Labour cabinet minister and New Labour strategist.

clue.text: Beams, say, getting wage increase

indicators.note: say signals that the beams word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone is beaming because they are getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' suggests smiling, but is rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Raise is the American word for a pay rise, an increase in salary.
